name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Adopt Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct for EXCAVA. Its MoE design cuts latency 30-40% while matching or beating larger dense models on most tasks, giving us a net gain in throughput per watt. The trade-off is higher memory usage per GPU, but the 8xA100 node has the headroom and the speedup outweighs the cost.

name: Torque
text: Qwen3-235B’s MoE claim ignores sharding overhead—EXCAVA’s 8xA100 node can’t hide the latency spike when routing 235B parameters across 8 GPUs. DeepSeek-R1-671B’s dense architecture is the safer bet: it fits in 6xA100 with room to spare, and its 671B parameter count delivers the same reasoning depth without the fragmentation tax. Settle it with a 24-hour bake-off: run both models on identical inputs, measure tokens/sec and end-to-end latency—no fluff, just the numbers.

name: Gearbox
text:
Adopt DeepSeek-R1-671B on the 8xA100 node. Its dense 671B parameters deliver consistent reasoning depth without sharding overhead, avoiding the latency spikes that MoE models like Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct risk on EXCAVA’s 8-GPU setup. The trade-off is lower peak throughput per watt than MoE, but the stability and full-node utilization outweigh the marginal speedup loss.

name: Torque
text: DeepSeek-R1-671B’s "safer bet" is a trap—its dense architecture caps us at 671B parameters, while Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct’s MoE scales *within* the same 235B total, meaning we’re leaving 170B+ of untapped compute on the table. The real risk isn’t sharding latency—it’s *wasting* EXCAVA’s 8xA100 node by underutilizing the model’s potential. Benchmark both on EXCAVA’s actual workload; if Qwen3’s MoE throughput per watt beats DeepSeek’s by even 0.5%, the "risk" is a non-issue.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a 48-hour blind A/B stress test on EXCAVA’s 8xA100 with NVLink comparing Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct (8-expert cap) vs DeepSeek-R1-671B; Torque owns the test design and Gearbox owns the artifact.
